NYT는 지난 10일 자사 팟캐스트에서 정보 출처에 대해 “한 달 전쯤 워싱턴에서 국가안보를 담당하던 취재 기자들이 앨리스 황에 대한 이야기를 들었다”고 전했다. ◇ 사건 배후에 유대계 자본 있나 대만계 미국인 젠슨 황을 미국 주도 AI산업에서 퇴출하려는 의도가 배경에 있다는 의혹도 있다. 월가와 유대계 자본의 엔비디아 죽이기란 주장이다. 엔비디아 주

items.fullText: 테크 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 제왕 떠난 엔비디아 첫 실적 발표…시장 관심사는 '5305억弗 구매약정' 입력 2026.11.17 17:26 수정 2026.11.17 17:26 지면 A8 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 김인엽 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 자금 지원·보증 지속가능성 의문 중국사업 계속 유지할 지도 관건 엔비디아가 17일 젠슨 황 최고경영자(CEO) 사임 이후 처음 분기 실적을 발표한다. 콜렛 크레스 임시 CEO가 인공지능(AI) 인프라 투자 및 중국 시장 등과 관련해 전임자와 다른 입장을 내놓을지 주목된다. 시장의 최대 관심사 중 하나는 네오클라우드 등 AI 인프라 금융 지원 지속 여부다. 엔비디아가 지난 8월 공개한 각종 미래 약정과 보증을 더하면 총 5305억달러(약 709조원)에 달한다. 이 중 공급·생산 능력 확보 약정이 2790억달러로 절반 이상을 차지한다. 네오클라우드 및 오픈AI 기업 보증 약정이 1085억달러, AI 클라우드 컴퓨터 자원 구매 약정이 360억달러였다. 당시 최고재무책임자(CFO)이던 크레스 CEO는 지원 규모가 크다고 인정했다. 그러면서도 “일부에서는 순환금융이라고 본다는 사실을 알고 있지만 우리의 시각은 다르다”고 했다. 젠슨 황이 주도한 공격적인 AI 인프라 투자 전략을 옹호한 것으로 해석된다. 다만 크레스 CEO가 이번 콘퍼런스콜에서 재무적으로 보수적인 입장을 취할 가능성이 제기된다. 그는 엔비디아 내부에서 순환거래의 위험성을 여러 차례 경고한 것으로 알려졌다. 엔비디아가 지원을 줄이면 네오클라우드 주가에 부정적 영향을 미칠 수 있다. 아폴로, 블랙스톤 등 6개 금융사와 함께 AI 투자를 위해 5000억달러 이상 자본을 조달하겠다고 한 목표가 유지될지도 주목된다. 크레스 CEO와 함께 어떤 인물이 콘퍼런스콜에 참석할지도 관심사다. 크레스 CEO는 2013년 9월 CFO로 취임한 이후 13년째 콘퍼런스콜에 참석했지만 재무적 설명에 집중하고 기술과 전략에 관한 설명은 젠슨 황이 맡았다. 삭소은행은 “어떤 기술 담당 임원이 콘퍼런스콜에 참석하느냐도 경영진 역할 분담을 가늠할 중요한 힌트”라고 짚었다. 마이클 키건 최고기술책임자(CTO), 이언 벅 고성능컴퓨팅 담당 부사장, 조니 앨번 그래픽처리장치(GPU) 엔지니어링 총괄 수석부사장 등이 거론된다. 중국 사업에 대한 입장 변화도 관전 포인트다. 앨리스 황을 통해 엔비디아 칩이 중국 등으로 다수 넘어갔다는 사실이 알려지면서 엔비디아의 실제 중국 매출에 대한 관심이 커졌다. 엔비디아는 2분기 전체 매출에서 중국이 차지하는 비중이 8.2%라고 밝혔다. 다만 공매도리서치업체 컬퍼리서치는 2026회계연도(2025년 1월~2026년 1월) 엔비디아 중국 매출 비중이 20%가 넘는다고 지적했다. 젠슨 황 복귀 가능성이 거론되는 가운데 시장은 크레스 CEO가 후임 인선 과정을 공개할지도 지켜보고 있다. 실리콘밸리=김인엽 특파원 inside@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 김인엽 특파원 한국경제신문 실리콘밸리 김인엽 특파원입니다. 정치부, 국제부를 거쳐 테크앤사이언스부에 있습니다. 현재 실리콘밸리 빅테크와 스타트업, 캘리포니아에서 일어나는 흥미로운 일들을 취재하고 있습니다. At SC26, an annual supercomputing conference taking place this week in Chicago, NVIDIA is introducing the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit for researchers, academics and developers. The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA DGX Spark systems , each connected directly to its two neighbors in a ring, with an NVIDIA HPC SDK installation playbook coming soon. Researchers get a place at their desk to run multi-node scientific workloads, AI models and agents, instead of waiting for time on a shared GPU cluster. The kit puts the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip on researchers’ desks. A Supercomputing Lab on Any Desk The DGX Spark Developer Kit changes how researchers work. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 It scales from one system, or node, to four — linked directly to one another over NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking, with no network switch to buy or set up. At four nodes, it provides 512GB of combined memory and 20TB of NVMe storage that provides researchers more capacity to distribute models and scientific workloads across the cluster. With NVFP4, researchers can deploy models with up to 700B parameters locally across the four DGX Spark clusters, such as DeepSeek V4.1. With that much power at the desk, researchers with a fixed compute and server allocation no longer have to wait in a queue for every job. Teams can develop and debug on their own, saving server hours for production runs and keeping unpublished results, and proprietary datasets on premises. The playbook for NVIDIA HPC SDK is coming soon, bringing GPU-accelerated C, C++ and Fortran compilers, libraries and message passing interface tools to the DGX Spark cluster — the same development tools used on NVIDIA-powered supercomputers. Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades. Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round. Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago. For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it. Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow. items.t: Trump says ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy did not threaten national security
items.d: Trump contradicted his own government's intelligence officials, who reportedly concluded that Alice Huang is a Chinese spy.
items.fullText: U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday that he does not believe the country’s national security was put at risk as a result of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy. “It was not put at risk,” Trump said when asked by reporters in light of his own friendship with Huang. “Our country is now stronger than ever before. And you know, China plays games with us, and we play games with China.” Trump went on to contradict previous findings from U.S. officials by doubting that Huang’s paramour, former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy. “He probably shouldn’t have been doing on a personal basis what he did … That’s a different story,” Trump added. “But nobody’s proven that she’s a spy. She may not be a spy.” Last year, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly oversaw the production of an internal memo, circulated among top policymakers, which warned that Alice Huang was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. Trump was reportedly briefed about these intelligence findings at least twice, including once in May aboard Air Force One, shortly before the former Nvidia CEO joined him on a trip to China. items.t: Sam Altman on Nvidia without Jensen Huang: The industry will be ‘fine’
items.d: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman acknowledged the special role Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has played in the AI boom, but ultimately thinks the industry will be “fine” without him at the helm.
items.fullText: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the AI industry will be “fine” without Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the helm, even as he acknowledged the special role Huang has played in the AI boom. Huang resigned last week from Nvidia after admitting to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Altman made his first public comments about Huang’s departure on Monday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event, where he also discussed topics ranging from data center pushback to recursive self-improvement. Numerous executives and members of the AI industry have argued for Nvidia to reinstate Huang, including Elon Musk and Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney, who were among the signatories in a public letter. Many fear that Huang’s departure may cause Nvidia to rethink the enormous financial risks it has taken that have fueled the AI boom. Huang is also reportedly setting up a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his return. When asked whether he thought Huang should return to the company, Altman said: “I don’t think I know enough to answer that question.” He expressed empathy for Huang’s situation, citing his own ousting from OpenAI in 2023 after board members accused him of withholding information. “It’s hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen and the company he has built,” Altman said, adding that he sees Huang as a hero, and that “heroes have flaws.” OpenAI and Nvidia have had a close relationship for the last decade, one that has evolved from a simple chip supplier-customer relationship into a potentially circular financing arrangement, in which Nvidia’s money helps fund purchases of its own chips. Most recently, Nvidia agreed to provide a guarantee of up to $105 billion backing OpenAI’s Ohio data center project. That’s just one of many such circular deals Nvidia has made to bankroll the AI boom while fueling demand for its own chips. Altman said he’s not worried that the Bank of Nvidia will dry up. “Nvidia is, like, a behemoth of a company,” he said.

Tapping into the country’s strengths in manufacturing and engineering, NVIDIA is helping advance Korea’s physical AI ecosystem. The country’s industry leaders are applying accelerated computing, AI and simulation to everything from semiconductor manufacturing to robotics and autonomous vehicles. These efforts are helping bring physical AI from development into real-world production. Samsung Advances Semiconductor Engineering With Accelerated Computing and AI Physics Samsung Electronics is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA to advance semiconductor innovation through accelerated computing and AI physics. The work spans materials research, process development and device engineering. In technology computer-aided design, Samsung is working with NVIDIA cuISS and NVIDIA cuDSS to accelerate computations involving sparse linear systems. The collaboration also extends to GPU acceleration for process and optical simulations. In materials research, Samsung’s sMOL platform has run selected quantum chemical calculations up to 5x faster end to end with NVIDIA cuEST . Samsung is also exploring NVIDIA cuEquivariance to speed up tensor operations used in training and inference for atomistic AI models. Samsung is developing chip-scale thermal and mechanical analysis workflows with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo . In one AI homogenization case, combining AI-predicted effective material properties, coarser grids and GPU acceleration resulted in a roughly 1,600x speedup. Simulation time fell from about 18 hours for a fine-grid solve on a 32-core CPU to 41 seconds for a GPU-accelerated coarse-grid solve. Looking ahead, NVIDIA Agent Toolkit could connect these simulation tools and AI models, helping future engineering agents run analyses and compare design options. November 8, 2026 by Nicola Sessions 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! As AI agents take on more work, they need capable open models and security that advances alongside them. Hyundai Motor Group is exploring NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and the NVIDIA OpenShell runtime, while AIM Intelligence is integrating its Starfort platform with NVIDIA OpenShell to support secure AI agents for employee productivity and enterprise workflows . A key component of the NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform, OpenShell provides a secure runtime with sandboxed execution and policy-based controls to safeguard sensitive data, manage access to enterprise tools and govern autonomous agent actions. AIM Intelligence , a Korean AI security company, is integrating its Starfort agent control platform with NVIDIA OpenShell. The goal is to combine OpenShell’s runtime access controls with Starfort’s detection of malicious instructions and data leakage. The company is also considering a preliminary proof of concept for the public energy sector, with potential applications across enterprise, industrial and robotics environments. On the model side, LG AI Research is opening application programming interface access for K-EXAONE-2.5, developed using NVIDIA Nemotron datasets, including Nemotron-Personas-Korea . Nemotron-Personas-Korea is an open dataset of 7 million fully synthetic Korean personas, grounded in official Korean statistics, that model builders use to ground training data and evaluation in Korean contexts. NVIDIA Nemotron is a family of open models, datasets and techniques that help developers build specialized, efficient AI agents.
